## Abstract

*Brewed Behavior: An Analysis of Coffee Consumption* explores how coffee drinkers’ habits and demographics relate to their spending behavior. Using data from the Great American Coffee Taste Test, we examine whether daily coffee consumption, preferred coffee strength, and self-rated coffee expertise are associated with monthly coffee expenditure and willingness to pay a premium for a single cup. We also investigate differences in monthly spending across age, gender, and education groups. Through visualizations such as stacked bar charts, connected dot plots, and line graphs, we identify patterns that may help coffee shop owners and roasters understand their customers, identify promising customer segments, and make more informed decisions about pricing and marketing. Because the survey attracts people interested in specialty coffee, our findings describe patterns within the sample rather than representing all coffee drinkers.
